head: 07481358c2d7ccba6c2a85f1c11e288d3a825a1b
summary:
Verdict: clean. The change is what the design and the accepted critique dispositions asked for. Commit 0748135 changes two tracked files against base 6c57f0c:
- .taad/slices/SL-038/build-slice-2.json: a one-line change at line 108, O-030 "done": true to "done": false. Its how-text is untouched.
- docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md: 11 lines added and 2 removed. The O-030 entry sits in the person-run network check at :230-238, and :260-261 was reworded.

It also adds tests/bugs/SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1, and commits the repro stage's tests/bugs/O-030-ledger-discharge.Tests.ps1 unchanged.

What I ran:
- The acceptance repro exits 0.
- `SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1 -Case All` passes every check (C-002..C-005), exit 0.
- Mutant 1, O-030 set back to done:true, restored by bytes with a matching hash afterwards. The repro exited 1, C-003 failed on numstat and on the one-line check, and C-004 failed on 'done is false'.
- Mutant 2, the whole ledger rewritten CRLF→LF, done still false. The repro and C-003 both pass it. That is correct, not a gap: `git ls-files --eol` shows the ledger stored as LF in the index (i/lf) and checked out as CRLF only because the system gitconfig sets core.autocrlf=true. The rewrite is not a committed change. The builder's "CRLF is kept" describes the checkout, not the blob.
- The default Core.Tests suite: 374/374 passed in 29 s (exit 0). This matters because the builder said no xUnit test reads the changed files, and that is wrong. RigLockScopeWordingTests walks every .md and .ps1 under docs/ and tests/, so it reads the edited SL-020-scanner.md and both new tests/bugs scripts. It passes, so there is no consequence.
- Fitness: 59 rules hold.
- Afterwards: the tree has only the engine's own SL-062 records changed, and no test host is left running.

Other checks:
- StalledShareTests.cs is the only test carrying Trait Network=SMB-LOOPBACK, so the recorded command in the O-030 entry selects exactly the one baseline test.
- Commit 91c955d and O-008 still reading done:true in SL-038 build-slice-1.json confirm the builder's correction of the O-008 precedent (m2).
- The engine's SL-059 merge commit touched only its own .taad/slices/SL-059/ directory. So C-005's commit-subject scan (`^SL-062[ :]`) should keep meaning "this slice" after the merge.
- One build attempt, no send-backs, so this is not a loop.

Assumption: the bug report was only a title, so I took the slice brief, which is SL-038 code-review-2 m1's fix text, as the report.

Residual risk, all declared by the builder:
- The engine's own obligation store is not in this tree and may still hold O-030 as done:true. A re-export of SL-038 would revert the hand-edit and turn the repro red.
- Whether done:false in this file routes anything inside the engine cannot be shown from the worktree. M1's disposition allowed exactly that, and build filed it as an engine-side follow-up rather than claiming it.

Second round: Second round, read adversarially: one new minor finding. C-004's mirror detector in tests/bugs/SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1 recognises two of the three obligation-state shapes the engine writes into .taad records. There is no current consequence, because no SL-038 record carries O-030 in the missing shape today.

The miss, and how I confirmed it:
- Surveying every `{"key":"O-nnn", ...}` object under .taad/slices gives three shapes. Build records use `done` (445), code reviews use `discharged` (908), and validate records use `verified` (183).
- Find-O030 (line 154) and the assertions at lines 173-178 know only `done` and `discharged`.
- I dropped a temporary `.taad/slices/SL-038/zz-sl062-review-probe.json` holding `{"key":"O-030","verified":"yes"}` into the tree. `-Case C-004` printed 'every check held' and exited 0. The probe was then removed, and git status is back to only the engine's SL-062 records.
- SL-038's validate-slice-4.json carries only O-038 (verified:'no'), not O-030, so the obligation's substance still holds today.

Probed and holding:
- **C-002 indexing:** `$before[0]` / `$after[0]` index into a function output that PowerShell unrolls to a single object. That works, and the builder's comma-drop mutant proves the comparison is not vacuous.
- **Line endings in C-003:** C-003 splits `git show` lines and the working-tree lines the same way (`\r?\n`). A CRLF→LF-only rewrite passes it, which is correct: `git ls-files --eol` shows the ledger stored i/lf under core.autocrlf=true, so that rewrite is not a committed change. A BOM is caught.
- **C-004 section slice:** it finds the first '*The person-run network check.*' and '*When that pass goes stale.*' and fails loudly if they are out of order. It collapses whitespace before matching, so re-wrapping the prose does not break it.
- **C-005 paths:** `git log --no-merges --grep '^SL-062[ :]'` is anchored against SL-0620. Renames and deletions of guarded files land outside the allowlist or on the untouched check.
- **git stderr:** the LF-replacement warnings git prints do not abort the script, including when the caller redirects stderr (run with 2>&1: exit 0).
- **SL-038 layout:** SL-038 has no subdirectories, so the non-recursive Get-ChildItem misses nothing.
- **Wrong host:** under Windows PowerShell 5.1 the script throws on `[Convert]::ToHexString` and `ConvertFrom-Json -Depth`, so it fails loudly rather than passing.

The first round's results stand: repro exit 0, all ledger cases pass, 374/374 default suite, Fitness holds.

findings.claim: C-004 says 'Every copy of O-030's own state under .taad/slices/SL-038/ says it is not discharged', but its detector only recognises objects carrying `done` or `discharged`. The engine's validate-slice records hold obligation state as `{"key":"O-nnn","verified":...}`: 183 such entries under .taad/slices. A validate-shaped O-030 copy saying verified:'yes' is neither found nor listed, and C-004 passes. So the design's mirror case (a second copy of O-030's state elsewhere) is only covered for two of the engine's three record shapes. There is no consequence today, because SL-038's validate records carry O-038, not O-030. The test's stated guarantee is still wider than what it checks.
findings.evidence: tests/bugs/SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1:154 (`$names -contains 'done' -or $names -contains 'discharged'`) and :173-178. SL-038/validate-slice-4.json payload.obligations = [{"key":"O-038","verified":"no",...}]. I placed a temporary probe .taad/slices/SL-038/zz-sl062-review-probe.json containing {"key":"O-030","verified":"yes"} in the tree; `-Case C-004` printed 'every check held' and exited 0. The probe was removed afterwards.
findings.fix: At line 154, also accept `$names -contains 'verified'`. After line 178, add the matching assertion: `if ($node.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains 'verified') { Check (-not ($node.verified -eq $true -or [string]$node.verified -eq 'yes')) "$($copy.File): O-030 verified is not yes (it is $(Show $node.verified))" }`. Update the C-004 header comment to name all three shapes.

obligations.evidence: I ran `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/O-030-ledger-discharge.Tests.ps1` and it exited 0 ('OK: O-030 is correctly recorded as owed to the person, not discharged.'). The flip is at .taad/slices/SL-038/build-slice-2.json:108. The formal discharge still belongs to validate.

C-001 is the unmodified repro. At base 6c57f0c the engine measured exit 1. My own mutant, O-030 set back to done:true and restored by bytes with a matching hash, gave exit 1 again. The current tree gives exit 0.

tests/bugs/SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1:107-118 (C-002) parses O-030 from `git show 6c57f0c:<ledger>` and from the working tree, and checks the how-text ordinal-equal plus both phrases. It passed 6/6. `git diff 6c57f0c HEAD` shows only the done line changed, so the how-text is byte-identical.

C-003 (:122-144) passes, and `git diff --stat 6c57f0c HEAD` shows build-slice-2.json | 2 +-. On my done:true mutant, C-003 failed on both numstat and the one-line check. A CRLF→LF-only rewrite passes C-003, but the file is stored i/lf under core.autocrlf=true, so that rewrite is not a committed change.

C-004 (:148-197) walks every JSON under .taad/slices/SL-038 for key=O-030 objects that carry a done or discharged field. It finds build-slice-2.json (False) and code-review-2.json ('no'). My grep agrees that index.json holds O-030 only in a revoke list and validate-slice-4.json holds it only in prose. The engine's DB copy is outside the tree and is declared as a gap.
C-005 (:201-231) passes. `git diff --stat 6c57f0c HEAD` lists no file under src/, and neither StalledShareTests.cs nor Rig/SmbRig.cs. The repro's LF-normalised hash matches the pinned value.

The disposition allowed build to report the gap instead of proving routing. The build record says the engine store is outside the worktree, claims no routing, and files an engine-side follow-up (SL-062 index.json open items, lines 33 and 41). The human-facing route, docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:230-238, now carries O-030.

docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:230-238 adds '*O-030, owed to the person.*' inside 'The person-run network check' (:225-229, the N-001..N-004 record). It gives the full command on one line, 'about 70 s', and 'next to N-001 to N-004'.

SL-020-scanner.md:233-235 says 'this record is where O-030 is discharged' and that SL-038's own build record keeps done:false 'and is never set true'. That is consistent with the permanent repro. The stale contract line remains in design-slice-1.json and is declared.

The tracked diff touches only build-slice-2.json under .taad/slices/SL-038. C-004 lists the other slices' O-030 files (SL-024, SL-044, SL-047, SL-056) without judging them, and C-005 enforces the allowlist. I confirmed both in my run.

SL-020-scanner.md:235-237 says spike#55's run 'broke "No stage runs it" above and does not discharge O-030'. The brief/stack conflict and the mechanical-guard follow-up are in SL-062 index.json open items (lines 37, 45). One part rests on the builder alone: I did not re-run its read-only Get-SmbMapping count of 0 loopback mappings, because reading network state is outside what I may touch. The rig's own sweep removes leftover rig mappings in any case (SL-020-scanner.md:271-274).

SL-020-scanner.md:235-238 cites the spike: HEAD 6c57f0c, 1 of 1 passed in 66.2 s, not a discharge. :260-261 was reworded to 'No person has run StalledShareTests on the extracted rig (the one agent run ... does not count)'.

`git log -S '"O-008"' -- .taad/slices/SL-038` returns 91c955d, and SL-038 build-slice-1.json still has O-008 done:true (around line 112). So the builder's correction holds: the precedent was not a hand-edit. The deviation is recorded.
The restated rationale is in the build record deviations (SL-062 index.json:77). The edit itself was a single-line text change, not a round-trip: the diff is one line.

`git diff --stat 6c57f0c HEAD` gives build-slice-2.json 2 +- (1/1) and SL-020-scanner.md 13 (11/2). The other files are the new tests/bugs scripts and the engine's own SL-062 records, all admitted by C-005's allowlist.

cases.evidence: tests/bugs/O-030-ledger-discharge.Tests.ps1 reads the real ledger's O-030. At base it was done:true beside how-text containing 'NEVER run' and 'remains owed to the person', and the repro exited 1 (the engine's run, and my own restored mutant). It exits 0 on the fixed tree.

SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1 C-002 compares O-030's how-text at 6c57f0c with the edited working tree, ordinal, and checks both phrases and the {key,done,how} shape. The builder's comma-drop mutant failed it. C-003's line comparison covers raw bytes that the JSON decode would hide.

C-003 checks numstat against 6c57f0c, BOM, a single line-ending style, the line count, and exactly one differing line, which must be the line after '"key": "O-030",' going from true to false. It fails on my done:true mutant. A pure CRLF→LF rewrite passes, correctly, because the blob is stored LF (i/lf) and the rewrite is no committed change.

C-004 walks every JSON under .taad/slices/SL-038 for key=O-030 with done or discharged, and asserts on the actual second copy in the tree, code-review-2.json (discharged:'no'). By its recursion it would flag a done:true copy in any SL-038 JSON, including index.json. The one second copy it cannot reach is the engine's DB store, which is outside the tree. That limit is declared, and M1's disposition allows it.

C-005 gathers the slice's paths from its SL-062 commits and the uncommitted tree, and requires them to be on the allowlist, StalledShareTests.cs and SmbRig.cs to be absent, and the repro hash to match. The builder's SmbRig.cs CRLF-append mutant failed it. `git diff --stat 6c57f0c HEAD` confirms that no code path was touched.

drift: No undeclared departure found. All seven of the build's declared deviations match the tree. These are: no hand-off file in .taad/slices/SL-062/, the dropped 'later slice sets done:true', the mirror search scoped to SL-038, the O-008 precedent corrected, the m3 rationale restated, the reword at SL-020-scanner.md:260-261, and the new SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1. One thing for the next reader: design-slice-1.json still carries the superseded contract line ('O-030 can then be set done:true ... in a later slice') and the O-008 auth_model. What governs now is docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:230-238.

The build record says nothing in the xUnit tests reads either changed file. That is not true. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/RigLockScopeWordingTests.cs:42-57 reads every .md and .ps1 under docs/ and tests/, which covers the edited SL-020-scanner.md and both tests/bugs scripts. The claim was used to skip the default suite. I ran it: 374/374 pass, so there is no consequence here, but a later docs-only slice should not reuse the same reasoning.
unreviewed: .taad/slices/SL-062/critique-1.json, critique-review-1.json, design-slice-1.json, build-slice-1.json: the engine's own stage records, not builder code. They were not opened, following the index-first rule. The design and critique content was supplied in the brief.
